Executive summary

This report compares Mamba-xLSTM-Net against N-BEATS-xLSTM-RUL using the same reporting pipeline, metric definitions, plots, and merged configuration dump. The goal is to make the model trade-off visible: accuracy, bias, training stability, and runtime are read together rather than as isolated numbers.

  • Primary accuracy metrics: lower RMSE, MAE, and loss are better; higher R² is better.
  • PHM score convention: the project phm_score is higher-is-better, while Liu / paper-style phm_score_paper is lower-is-better.
  • Figure reading order: first inspect aggregate metrics, then training curves, then per-bearing prediction and residual plots to separate general accuracy from systematic bias.

Ablation & configuration comparison

The ablation section is the report's high-level scoreboard. Results are aggregated across 2 run(s) by matching the stable run_id prefix before the seed suffix. That makes repeated seeds comparable without hiding model or dataset identity.

How to read this section. Each metric is plotted on its own axis so scale does not mislead the comparison. Error bars show seed-level standard deviation where repeated runs exist. The best run is highlighted according to the metric direction: lower for loss/RMSE/MAE and Liu paper PHM score, higher for R² and project PHM score.

Comparison: Mamba-xLSTM-Net vs N-BEATS-xLSTM-RUL

This is a controlled model comparison on the same dataset and training protocol. The important difference is the architecture declared in model.name, so the metric table and paired figures should be read as an architecture-level trade-off.

Interpretation rule. Prefer the model that improves held-out test RMSE/MAE while preserving R² and residual shape. A checkpoint with excellent validation RMSE but poor held-out residuals is usually overfitting the validation bearings.

Per-bearing test predictions

Prediction plots are the most important qualitative check. Look for the model tracking the monotonic decline of true RUL, especially near end-of-life where maintenance decisions are most sensitive.

Per-bearing residuals over time

Residuals show model bias directly. Positive residuals mean the model predicts too much remaining life; negative residuals mean it is conservative.

Residuals (all test points)

The pooled residual plot summarizes systematic optimism or pessimism across all held-out test points.

Mamba-xLSTM-Net
N-BEATS-xLSTM-RUL

Residual histogram

A narrow residual distribution centered near zero is preferable. Skewed or heavy-tailed residuals indicate a model that fails only on specific lifecycle phases or bearings.

N-BEATS-xLSTM-RUL

Configuration (merged YAML)

The merged YAML is the reproducibility record. It captures the data split, windowing, model hyperparameters, optimizer settings, and seed used for each column.

Mamba-xLSTM-Net
data:
  dataset: xjtusy
  root: ../data-bearing/xtju-sy
  cache_dir: ../data-bearing/processed/xjtusy
  window_length: 32
  stride_train: 1
  stride_eval: 1
  label_scheme: linear
  smoothing_alpha: 0.1
  n_bands: 5
  batch_size: 256
  num_workers: 8
  train_bearings:
  - '1_1'
  - '1_2'
  - '1_3'
  - '2_1'
  - '2_2'
  val_bearings:
  - '1_4'
  test_bearings:
  - '1_5'
  - '2_3'
model:
  name: mamba_xlstm_net
  d_model: 128
  xlstm_blocks: 3
  slstm_positions:
  - 1
  xlstm_heads: 4
  xlstm_force_fallback: false
  mamba_blocks: 2
  mamba_d_state: 128
  mamba_d_conv: 4
  mamba_expand: 2
  mamba_headdim: 64
  mamba_n_groups: 1
  mamba_rope_fraction: 0.5
  mamba_is_mimo: false
  mamba_mimo_rank: 4
  mamba_chunk_size: 64
  mamba_is_outproj_norm: false
  mamba_bidirectional: true
  mamba_backend: auto
  fusion: gated
  head_hidden: 64
  dropout: 0.1
train:
  max_epochs: 75
  lr: 0.0008
  weight_decay: 0.0003
  xlstm_lr_mult: 0.75
  freeze_xlstm_epochs: 5
  scheduler: cosine
  warmup_epochs: 5
  monotonicity_weight: 0.05
  gradient_clip_val: 1.0
  early_stopping_patience: 9999
  precision: bf16-mixed
  seed: 42
  results_root: results
  run_id: null
